title: "Perhaps He Will Heed": The Same Hope God Held for Pharaoh and for a Blind Beggar
excerpt: A third man 'comes running' in the Quran — the blind man of Surah ʿAbasa (80:8, jāʾaka yasʿā) — and unlike the two runners received as heroes, he is met with a frown. God's rebuke rests on a single clause: 'perhaps he will purify himself, or heed' (80:3). It is the same clause God gave Musa for approaching Pharaoh: 'perhaps he will heed, or fear' (20:44). The mightiest tyrant and the lowliest seeker, handed to God's messengers under one identical hope.
seo_title: Perhaps He Will Heed: Pharaoh and the Blind Man Share One Clause (80:3, 20:44)
seo_description: In Surah ʿAbasa, God rebukes the Prophet's frown at a blind seeker with 'perhaps he will heed' (80:3) — the same clause He gave Musa for Pharaoh (20:44). A corpus-verified reading of how God levels the tyrant and the beggar under one hope.
